body: Working on spreading the word to all my developer friends. This has the true spirit of the original but with more protections in place, and an active steward to answer questions.

Two corrections to the request above:
- Full name, matching the license's title exactly: DO WHAT THE FUCK YOU WANT TO, WHEN YOU WANT TO PUBLIC LICENSE, Version 1 (the form dropped the comma and the version).
- GitHub's Markdown stripped two placeholders from item 3. The per-entity JSON is at `data.snvrkotics.com/entity/<id>.json` and `dripgraph.com/ld/<page>.json`.

Answers to the questions I'd expect on this request, so reviewers have them up front.

### Does clause 2 impose a condition?

No. Clause 3 tells the reader to ignore clause 2, so nothing after clause 1 is a requirement, and using the work never depends on following them. This was deliberate, to avoid the problem the JSON license's "Good, not Evil" clause created.

### What grants the permission: clause 0 or clause 1?

Clause 0 is the grant, exactly as in the WTFPL. Clause 1 doesn't replace it. It states what the WTFPL leaves unsaid: wherever the law won't let the author simply give the work away, the grant is free, worldwide, permanent and irrevocable, covering everything the law allows. Those are the same terms as CC0-1.0's fallback license.

### How is this different from WTFPL and WTFNMFPL under the matching guidelines?

Two substantive clauses that neither has:

| | Explicit irrevocable, worldwide grant | Warranty and liability disclaimer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WTFPL | No | No |
| WTFNMFPL | No | Liability only |
| **W2FPL-1.0** | **Yes (clause 1)** | **Yes (clause 4)** |

The title also differs. It isn't a rename with cosmetic edits.

### Is it OSD/FSD-compliant?

It places no conditions on use, modification or redistribution, and has no field-of-use limits, attribution or notice requirement. Clause 4 only disclaims warranty and liability, as nearly every permissive license does.

### "The author" and "the W2FPL coauthors"?

The copyright line credits the license text itself to its author and to future coauthors, meaning people whose proposals go into later versions. There are none yet. In clauses 1 and 4, "the author" means the author of the licensed work, as in the WTFPL. The copyright line is the license's own copyright notice, so it can be marked as copyright text in the XML, as SPDX does for the WTFPL.

### Can the text change?

Version 1 is final. As steward I commit to never modifying it, and to publishing any change as a new, separately numbered version at its own URL (which would need its own identifier). The preamble lets anyone else modify the license only under a new name, so derivatives can't be confused with it.

### Why `W2FPL-1.0`?

"W2FPL" is the license's own short name ("when 2 fuck"), used on its site, badge and repository. `-1.0` follows the usual SPDX convention for version 1. I'm happy to use whatever form you prefer.

### Is it a vanity or single-project license?

No. Nothing in it is specific to a person, project or company, and it applies to any kind of work. It's developed in public at https://github.com/snvrk/w2fpl, where anyone can propose changes through issues and pull requests. Its first uses are two datasets I publish; I'll add links here as other projects adopt it.

### Is there a relationship with the WTFPL's author?

No. The WTFPL permits modified versions under a new name, which is what this is. It doesn't claim to be a WTFPL version and doesn't use the WTFPL's name or badge.

### The XML

Drafts are at https://github.com/snvrk/w2fpl/tree/main/spdx (`W2FPL-1.0.xml` and the test text). I'll update them to whatever markup you want, such as replaceable or omittable sections.

I'm joining the SPDX legal mailing list and can be on the call whenever this comes up.

The paper on the license is now published on Zenodo:

Gottfried, C. (2026). *Do What You Want, Permanently: The W2FPL, a WTFPL Derivative with an Explicit Irrevocable Grant and a Warranty Disclaimer.* https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23121447

It covers the clause-by-clause analysis, a comparison with WTFPL, WTFNMFPL, CC0-1.0, the Unlicense, 0BSD and MIT-0, and the license's limitations, including an open question about when clause 1's condition applies (Section 7). The paper itself is released under the W2FPL.
